lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: asking for help before a crisis

objective: Learners write what an early ask for help would actually sound like across four fictional scenarios at different concern levels, so asking early becomes a rehearsed script rather than something invented under pressure.
scenario: Given four fictional scenarios at mild, moderate, moderate-serious, and serious concern levels, the learner writes what an early ask for help would sound like for each, contrasted with what waiting until crisis would look like.
safetyNotes: All four scenarios are fictional; no real personal concern needs to be disclosed to complete this lesson.
This lesson does not diagnose or advise on any real situation — it practices the wording of an early ask, not the specifics of any real concern.
materials: the provided four fictional scenarios and concern-level scale

tasks.directions: Before writing, guess why people wait too long to ask for help even when they know they should ask sooner.

prompts.text: Why do you think people often wait longer than they should to ask for help, even when part of them knows they should ask sooner?

tasks.directions: Write an early-ask script for the mild and moderate scenarios.

prompts.text: I wrote an early-ask script for the mild-concern scenario.
I wrote an early-ask script for the moderate-concern scenario.

tasks.directions: Write early-ask scripts for the moderate-serious and serious scenarios, and contrast one with what waiting would look like.

prompts.text: Write early-ask scripts for the remaining two scenarios. Then, for one of the four, write a contrasting sentence showing what it would sound like if the person waited until crisis instead.

tasks.directions: Reflect on your own concern-level threshold.

prompts.text: At which concern level do you personally tend to actually ask for help — mild, moderate, or later? Is that where you'd want it to be?

remediation: If all four early-ask scripts sound identical regardless of concern level (no difference in urgency or directness), reteach by contrasting a clearly mild-toned ask with a clearly serious-toned ask side by side, then have the learner revise each script to match its actual concern level.
extension: Have the learner write a fifth, self-invented scenario at an even higher concern level than the four provided, and write its early-ask script.
